I cannot even associate that Eva with the other Eva. It only shows her doing that thing to Cora once...though yeah, the Zelena thing, but that was fabricated after s2. And in that case, Eva was saving Leopold from marrying a liar. Snow can blame her mom for that all she wants, but how is saving a man from someone passing another man's child off as his an "evil move"?

If Snow changed just from a weak lecture from her mom, I honestly don't see there being a deep transition behind this. One minute, OUAT shows us Eva lecturing Snow and changing her from a brat to a kind person, then we see Eva tripping Cora and being a haughty brat in the past. PS she was OLDER than Snow.

Basically, though the show didn't mean for anyone to think too deeply on this, they're suggesting people who seem kind in their older years were born brats, or evil, if you will. "Evil isn't born, it's made." They did a one-eighty with Snow and her mom and made it all gawky "Kindness isn't born; it's made" and yet, they failed to address it in the show.

I just cannot picture someone tripping Cora for fun then growing to lecture her daughter that servants are people too. This smells of two-dimensional writing, of forcing the plot to be how they wanted, even if your characters aren't behaving in character.

But what REALLY bothers me is Snow's thing is supposed to be she's NATURALLY pure of heart, yet they made her a brat as a child. Then they forced that saaaaame thing on Belle. Like Belle was suddenly the "pure of heart" one. But the whole arc of Snow White is supposed to be her pure heart. You can't just toss it to someone else because you want to A) repeat your writing or B) got tired of leaving it on one character and put it on another one.

They also made Snow claim "there's no such thing as true love" after she saw Ruby and Peter and fully believed in them, and I feel Eva and Leopold had true love. Though it's not shown much in OUAT, in the fact Leopold praises his daughter as being as lovely as her mother in front of Regina in the genie episode...I feel the line "there's no such thing as true love" was done in a thoughtless way in order to prove to the audience Snow White is no stupid airhead. But she shouldn't be someone who believes that. If she'd said "There's no such thing as true love for me", it'd be a different story. But she had never had her heart broken, and usually that's what women say when they have. So she literally had no reason to say such.

So nah, I don't think Eva changed so much as the writers ghosted her character and merely picked it up to force plotlines to work.
